daily_brief: The day's most significant developments center on escalating climate emergencies and fragile diplomatic openings. Catastrophic wildfires across southwestern France and Spain have displaced over 325,000 people, with flames now within 15 kilometers of Bordeaux as another heatwave approaches [RFI, France 24, The Hindu]. President Macron has convened a crisis cabinet meeting. Meanwhile, a tentative pause in hostilities between the US and Iran—marking the second consecutive day without strikes—has sent oil prices tumbling more than 7% and opened a narrow window for renewed negotiations [France 24, Le Monde, Financial Times, The Hindu]. In Berlin, a 24-hour manhunt ended when police shot and killed Abdul Ballout, the suspect in Saturday's Pride attack that killed one and injured 29; German authorities have characterized the incident as an Islamist terror attack [BBC, RFI]. India's student protest movement secured a rare political victory as Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following weeks of demonstrations over exam system failures [BBC, France 24, Al Jazeera]. In financial markets, Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT surged 465% in its Shanghai debut, surpassing Intel's market capitalization in Asia's largest IPO of the year [Nikkei Asia, Financial Times].

top_stories.headline: Wildfires Displace Over 325,000 Across France and Spain as Heatwave Looms
bullets: More than 220,000 people evacuated in France's Gironde department, with fires now 15 km from Bordeaux; 75,000+ evacuated in Spain across Ávila, Madrid and Toledo provinces
French President Macron convened crisis cabinet meeting Monday; Spanish PM Sánchez visited fire-hit areas in Valencia where new blaze forced 15,000 additional evacuations
Combined burned area exceeds 146,000 hectares; Spanish Interior Minister described Ávila fire as a 'monster' with 280 km perimeter
Temperatures forecast to reach 37-40°C in Bordeaux region later this week, complicating firefighting efforts

top_stories.headline: Berlin Pride Attack Suspect Shot Dead After Islamist Terror Probe Launched
bullets: Abdul Ballout, 21, German citizen with Lebanese heritage, killed by police in Spandau after charging officers with a knife following 24-hour manhunt
Saturday attack near Tiergarten park killed one woman and injured at least 29 when van drove into crowd followed by stabbing
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt confirmed evidence points to Islamist terror attack; suspect had prior criminal record and attempted to join ISIS in 2025
Ballout had been arrested in Lebanon in July 2025, sentenced to three months for incitement, before returning to Germany
